<reason>Both sides built genuinely strong, well-structured cases with clean pressure-question exchanges that both answered in proper A1/A2 format. CON's strongest moves were the bait-and-switch charge (PRO's "staged trials" quietly substitute non-driving constructs for the self-sustaining drives the motion is actually about) and the concrete cage-based recall proposal, which blunted PRO's claim that reversibility testing is impossible in principle. CON's sovereignty/consent argument was also vivid and pointed. But PRO's core throughline — that a demand for "proven recall in practice" of a self-sustaining drive is structurally the same unfalsifiable, ever-shiftable standard as the "ecological certainty" CON claims to reject — was never squarely defused. CON kept restating the standard (contained, reversible in practice, regionally agreed) without ever specifying what evidence short of the irreversible act itself would satisfy it, and never returned to rebut PRO's direct closing charge that this amounts to a permanent veto dressed as caution. PRO also successfully neutralized much of the "impossible sequencing" pressure by grounding its case in a genuine staged-evidence framework (self-limiting → split-drive → self-sustaining), which is a coherent middle path rather than a strawman. CON's strongest point (natural harm doesn't license engineered harm without consent, B2.7) was left unanswered by PRO, which costs PRO some ground, but it wasn't enough to overturn PRO's cleaner closing crystallization of the decisive asymmetry: certain, ongoing mortality versus a standard CON could never actually satisfy. The debate was close and both sides argued with skill, but PRO's framing proved slightly more resilient under the mutual cross-examination.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The most decisive exchange was CON's B4.1/B4.2 answers to PRO's pressure questions (proposing outdoor-cage recall testing and drawing the self-limiting/self-sustaining line) versus PRO's closing charge in A5.1-A5.2 that CON's "proven recall in practice" standard for self-sustaining drives is itself unfalsifiable and functions as a permanent veto — a charge CON never specifically rebutted with a concrete satisfiable benchmark.</best_rebuttal>
